defects: The copy card ('ONE API CALL. INSTANT SETTLEMENT. A WEBHOOK... EVERY STATE CHANGE.') is cut off at both frame edges. The first letters are lost ('NE', 'ETTLEMENT', 'VERY'), and in the pairs the line looks like it wraps around ('INSTANTNE'), so it reads as a layout bug and not a deliberate crop.
The copy card is a flat, frontal, nearly static hold of body text. It is dead air in a 15 s piece, and it explains in words what the board metaphor already showed.
The wide board shot is a locked-off, frontal hold. Only one row is changing (the 09:41 row scrambling) while the rest of the frame sits still.

At 1:1, the half-flipped flaps leave faint ghost glyph fragments over the digits (around the '4', '1' and '5'), and the glyphs are slightly soft. They look like a texture swap, not real flap geometry with a thickness edge.
The lighting is a low-contrast near-black falloff with crushed shadows. The flaps have almost no specular response or depth, so the board looks more like a CG preset than a physical object.
The tilted close-ups (DELAYED, PENDING, SETTLED) use the same angled-board camera move with a different word each time. They read as interchangeable, and the camera has no motivated push or rack.
Pace fails the benchmark: the longest shot is 3.2 s and the median 2.4 s, against a world-class median of about 2 s, with holds on text cards that have no reason to last that long.
gaps: Motion: the flap physics has no weight or cascade choreography. Top work would ripple the state change down the board with staggered overshoot, settle and bounce, sell the SETTLED moment as one big wave or wipe that is clearly the peak (around 60–70%), and use camera moves that react to the flips. Here the camera repeats the same tilt-and-hold.

Sound: the flap clatter bursts line up with the flips, and a tonal bed comes in from about 6 s, but the arrangement is blocky. It switches between clatter and drone sections with static tonal partials and no clear build into the resolve. There is no designed silence or single signature hit before the 'DELAYS: NONE' resolve.

Finish: the flaps need real modelled thickness, edge highlights, slight per-flap irregularity, motion blur on the flip and graded light with depth. The text-heavy copy card should be replaced by staging the message on the board itself, framed so nothing is clipped.
